title: CathedralAction
description: One step of a desktop trace. The agent emits exactly one of these per turn; the executor performs `action`, and the distillation pipeline trains on `reasoning` + `action` together. Strict mode: every object forbids additional properties, so a non-conforming token stream is rejected at the provider rather than discovered by the grader.

step.description: Zero-based index of this step within the trace.

reasoning.description: Why this action, written for a reader who cannot see the screen. Name the target element, say what ruled out the plausible alternatives, and state the expected result. This is the primary training signal.

observation_ref.description: Digest of the observation this action was chosen from (sha256:...). Binds the action to exactly what the agent could see, so a replay can present the same input.

Action.description: Tool names mirror the computer-use-linux MCP surface. Hermes registers them as mcp_computer_use_linux_<tool>; the bare name is stored so traces stay portable across harnesses.

element_index.description: Accessibility element index from the most recent get_app_state. Preferred over coordinates: indices survive window movement, coordinates do not, and a coordinate-based trace cannot be replayed on a different resolution.

selector.description: Semantic selector for the target element, when an index is unavailable.

coordinates.description: Desktop pixel coordinates. Last resort only; a trace that relies on these is weaker training data and harder to grade.

text.description: Literal text for type_text, or the value for set_value.

keys.description: Key or chord for press_key, e.g. 'ctrl+s'.

target_window.description: Window selector for activate_window, or to target input at a specific window.

action_name.description: AT-SPI action for perform_action: Press, Activate, Toggle, and so on. Defaults to the element's primary action.

outcome_claim.description: For done and blocked only: what was observed that proves the task succeeded, or what specifically prevents progress. An unobserved claim here is the single most damaging thing an agent can write, because a trace that passes its predicate for the wrong reason teaches the wrong lesson.
